section: Educational Psychology · Ch11 — Special Needs & Inclusive Education
subject: Educational Psychology
stem: A student consistently struggles to sit still, is easily distracted even during simple tasks, frequently interrupts others, and finds it hard to follow multi-step instructions across all classes. These persistent difficulties with attention and impulse control are characteristic of:
explanation: ADHD is characterised by persistent inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity across multiple settings — distinct from dyslexia (a reading-specific learning disability) or cerebral palsy (a motor disorder).

section: Educational Psychology · Ch11 — Special Needs & Inclusive Education
subject: Educational Psychology
stem: A child born with an extra copy of chromosome 21, showing characteristic facial features and some degree of intellectual disability, has a genetic condition called:
explanation: Down Syndrome results from an extra copy of chromosome 21 (trisomy 21), causing characteristic physical features and varying degrees of intellectual disability — a distinct genetic condition from cerebral palsy (a motor disorder from brain injury) or autism.

section: Educational Psychology · Ch11 — Special Needs & Inclusive Education
subject: Educational Psychology
stem: For a student with significant hearing impairment, which of the following classroom strategies is MOST appropriate?

options.option_text: Seating the student near the front, facing the teacher, with visual aids and clear lip movement
Seating the student at the very back of the classroom
Relying purely on audio recordings with no visual support
Excluding the student from group discussions entirely

explanation: Front seating facing the teacher, visual aids, and clear articulation (supporting lip-reading) are standard, effective accommodations for hearing-impaired students in an inclusive classroom.

section: Educational Psychology · Ch11 — Special Needs & Inclusive Education
subject: Educational Psychology
stem: For a student with significant visual impairment, which classroom accommodation is MOST appropriate?

options.option_text: Braille materials, audio recordings, and tactile learning aids
Only visual worksheets with small print
Removing the student from all practical activities
Requiring the student to copy from the blackboard only

explanation: Braille materials, audio resources, and tactile aids are standard accommodations for visually impaired students, ensuring access to the same curriculum through non-visual channels.
